title: The rupee in 2026: a record slide, then a rebound
dek: From near 89 to the dollar in January to a record low near 96.90, then a rebound in November. What moved the rupee this year.
seoTitle: Rupee vs dollar 2026: record lows and the rebound
status: Falls 60 paise on oil and a firmer dollar
bigLabel: Rupees per US dollar at the close on 27 Nov (PTI, provisional). Eight-month high of 92.20 on 25 Nov; record closing low 96.88 on 8 Oct.

glance.what: The rupee hit a string of record lows in 2026, with a record closing low of 96.88 per dollar on 8 October. It strengthened for most of November. On 25 November it closed at 92.20, per PTI's revised figure: an eight-month high that erased its losses since April. It then slipped for two days, closing at 92.98 (provisional) on 27 November, down 60 paise, as oil prices rose and the dollar firmed.
glance.why: A weaker rupee makes imports like oil, electronics and foreign travel or education more expensive, and adds to inflation.
glance.next: Falling oil prices, foreign inflows and RBI dollar sales have helped. A stronger dollar on US rate-rise bets, or a renewed oil spike, would push the other way.

forYou: Anything priced in dollars costs more: foreign trips, overseas tuition, imported gadgets. Families receiving money from abroad get more rupees per dollar or dirham.
next: Watch oil prices and foreign investor flows.

events.title: First record low of the year
events.summary: The rupee weakens toward 91.7 per dollar as foreign investors sell Indian stocks.

events.title: Past 92 as war in West Asia lifts oil
events.summary: Soaring oil prices and fighting in the Gulf push the rupee past 92 for the first time.

events.title: A lifetime low of 93.96
events.summary: Global uncertainty drives the rupee to a new record.

events.title: Through 96 as oil surges
events.summary: The rupee hits 96.25 in early trade after closing below 96 for the first time the previous Friday. Foreign investors pulled nearly $20 billion from Indian equities in the first four months of 2026.

events.title: Hovering near record lows ahead of the RBI decision
events.summary: The rupee trades around 96.4 per dollar. The RBI keeps selling dollars to slow the fall, and markets price in a rate hike.

events.title: RBI steps in; the rupee turns
events.summary: After the RBI sells dollars and tightens currency rules, the rupee rises nearly 1% in October, one of Asia's best performers that month, and settles around 94.46 on 5 November.

events.title: A six-month high of 93.70
events.summary: The rupee touches 93.70 per dollar in early trade, its strongest in about six months, as crude falls and foreign money flows back in. It has recovered more than 3% from its record low near 96.90, and closes the day at 93.93.

events.title: A small pullback from the high
events.summary: The rupee slips 41 paise to close at 94.12 on 12 November as the dollar strengthens, then edges up to 94.05 in early trade on 13 November on foreign inflows and softer oil. One forex adviser still sees the broader trend favouring the rupee.

events.title: Slips to 94.20 on US rate worries
events.summary: The rupee falls 8 paise to close at 94.20 per dollar (provisional). Dealers point to a stronger dollar after higher-than-expected US inflation data, which raised bets that the US Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December, and to falling Indian shares.

events.title: Edges up to 94.13 as oil eases
events.summary: The rupee rises 6 paise to 94.13 per dollar in early trade on Monday, after closing Friday at 94.19 (final figure). Forex traders credit lower crude oil prices and rising Indian shares, while a strong dollar, rising US bond yields and US-Iran tension limit the gain.

events.title: Rises to 93.63 as oil falls and foreign money flows in
events.summary: The rupee closed Monday 25 paise stronger at 93.94 per dollar, then opened at 93.72 on Tuesday and touched 93.63 in early trade, PTI reports. Dealers credit lower oil prices, which ease India's import bill, and foreign investors buying Indian shares: they bought ₹4,864.68 crore of shares on Monday alone, according to exchange data. Moneycontrol links the inflows to investors moving money away from AI-linked trades elsewhere.
events.differs: Moneycontrol gives Monday's close as 93.93 and Tuesday's opening as 93.73; PTI gives 93.94 and 93.72.

events.title: Rupee crosses 93 and closes at a seven-month high of 92.67
events.summary: The rupee closed at 92.67 per dollar on Friday (provisional), 65 paise stronger than Thursday and its strongest level in seven months, PTI reports. During the day it crossed 93 for the first time since 20 April, per Business Today. Dealers credit foreign investors buying Indian shares, lower oil prices (Brent fell 1.82% to $90.31 during the day, per PTI) and a rally in Indian stocks. Business Today says foreign investors have put about $12 billion into Indian shares this month, and also points to exporters selling dollars and possible RBI action. On the two days before, PTI reported closes of 93.44 (provisional) on Wednesday and 93.32 on Thursday.
events.differs: NewsBytes gives 92.68 for Friday. PTI's own report gives the gain as both 65 and 67 paise. For Thursday, PTI gives a close of 93.32; Kotak Neo gives 93.29 in one place and 93.32 in another. For the 17 Nov close, Business Today gives 93.47.

events.title: Forex reserves fall $14.2 billion to a three-month low; rupee on track for its best month in eight years
events.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $14.20 billion to $705.34 billion in the week to 13 November, the lowest in about three months, RBI data released on Friday show, per The Tribune and Moody's via TradingView. Foreign currency assets fell $7.90 billion and gold holdings $6.18 billion. Forex reserves are the dollars, other currencies and gold the RBI holds, partly to steady the rupee. Separately, Business Standard reports the rupee is up 2.46% in November so far, on course for its best monthly gain in more than eight years, helped by nearly $13 billion of foreign investment.
events.status: Official data · RBI; Market data · Business Standard
events.differs: Business Standard gives Friday's close as 92.68; PTI gives 92.67 (provisional).

numbers.k: Rupee gain in Nov so far

events.title: Rupee ends its rally, closing 30 paise weaker at 92.92 as Indian shares fall
events.summary: The rupee settled 30 paise weaker at 92.92 per dollar on Monday (provisional), PTI reports via Telangana Today. It had strengthened to 92.43 early on, helped by cheaper oil, but weakened as Indian shares fell sharply; it touched 93.11 during the day. A dealer at Mirae Asset Sharekhan linked the fall to the drop in Indian shares. A firm US dollar, near a 19-month high, also weighed, per Angel One. Brent crude was at $92.08 a barrel, down 0.53%. Angel One describes the move as the rupee easing slightly from a seven-month high.
events.differs: PTI reports differ on Monday's opening rate: 92.47 in the closing report (Telangana Today) and 93.47 in the early-trade report (HDFC Sky). Angel One gives a level of 92.9160 at 6:09 pm. Business Standard put the day's low at 93.08 at 12:30 pm; PTI gives 93.11. PTI's final figure for Friday's close is 92.62; its provisional figure on Friday was 92.67.

events.title: Rupee rises 69 paise to close at 92.16, an eight-month high that erases its losses for the financial year
events.summary: The rupee opened at 92.65 per dollar on Wednesday and closed at 92.16 (provisional), up 69 paise from Monday's close of 92.85, PTI reports. PTI calls it the rupee's highest level this year and an eight-month high; it wipes out all the rupee's losses since the financial year began in April. The rupee has gained in five straight sessions since 94.19 on 13 November. Currency markets were shut on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti. Analysts quoted by PTI credit strong buying in Indian shares, foreign investor inflows, cheaper crude and RBI steps to improve dollar supply; a firm US dollar limited the gains. Foreign investors bought a net ₹5,672.99 crore of Indian shares on Monday, per exchange data cited by PTI. Brent crude was at $91.55 a barrel. A stronger rupee makes imports such as fuel and foreign travel slightly cheaper.
events.differs: PTI's afternoon report gave a best level of 92.29; DSIJ put the best level at 92.18 and InCred Money at 92.21. AIR News first reported a close of 92.23, then 92.16. The 92.16 close is provisional. PTI's final figure for Monday's close is 92.85, not the provisional 92.92 shown earlier.

events.title: Rupee slips 24 paise to 92.44 as oil rises and US tariff worries weigh
events.summary: The rupee opened at 92.50 per dollar on Thursday and closed at 92.44 (provisional), down 24 paise, PTI reports. It moved between 92.31 and 92.66 during the day. Forex traders blamed higher crude oil prices and worries over the proposed US tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods; foreign investor inflows limited the fall. Rajeev Sharan of Brickwork Ratings said Brent crude climbing back above $95 a barrel and the tariff proposal were the two pressures. Brent was at $93.80 a barrel in futures trade at the time of the report. Foreign investors bought a net ₹4,479.08 crore of Indian shares on Wednesday, per exchange data. PTI now gives Wednesday's close as 92.20, up 65 paise, not the provisional 92.16 shown earlier.
events.differs: PTI's afternoon report gives a provisional close of 92.44, down 24 paise; a later Millennium Post report says the rupee settled at 92.38, down 18 paise.

events.title: Rupee falls 60 paise to 92.98 as oil climbs and the dollar firms
events.summary: The rupee opened at 92.44 per dollar on Friday and closed at 92.98 (provisional), down 60 paise, PTI reports. It touched 93.01 during the day, its weakest level of the session. Anuj Choudhary of Mirae Asset Sharekhan said crude oil rose after reports that Houthis attacked a Saudi Aramco facility, and also pointed to a firmer dollar and month-end dollar demand from importers. Brent crude was at $97.19 a barrel in futures trade, and the dollar index at 103.77. Kaveri More of Choice Broking said record foreign share purchases in November, of $15.16 billion, had supported the rupee. Foreign investors bought a net ₹5,843.33 crore of Indian shares on Thursday. The Sensex fell 1.17% and the Nifty 1.07% on Friday. PTI notes the rupee had recovered nearly 5% from its record closing low of 96.88 on 8 October.
events.differs: PTI's Friday report gives Thursday's close as 92.38, after an 18-paise fall; its Thursday report had given a provisional close of 92.44, down 24 paise.
